_comment: Taxonomy behind the directory's topic pages (/topics/<id>/): the subcategory and task layer that mirrors the way tool directories such as Futurepedia group listings, mapped to agent skills. groups mirror a tool directory's top-level sections; topics are its subcategories, tags and tasks. A skill matches a topic when its name matches name_re, its folder path matches path_re, or its summary (scope "summary", the default) or whole description (scope "description") matches text_re and its category is in categories. exclude lists skills (owner/repo/slug) that mention the topic only in passing. A topic publishes a page when at least 3 listed skills match; unpublished topics stay on the topics hub with their count and a listing request link. futurepedia records the tool-directory labels each entry stands in for, for the parity audit. Copy follows the sales-copy standard: no em dashes, no invented proof.

topics.name: Customer Service
topics.intro: Customer service skills help an agent keep customers and answer them well: churn risk detection from support tickets and NPS, cancel flows and save offers, win-back research and support queue handling in Google Workspace. They turn scattered support signals into a list of accounts to act on and the next message to send.
guide: Separate the retention playbooks from the operational skills. Churn prevention skills are Markdown procedures for cancel flows, save offers and dunning, so they run with no setup; the support persona skill works inside Gmail and Google Workspace and needs that account authorized.

Signal skills such as the churn risk detector read support tickets, Slack channels and usage data. Check the Before you install panel for the data sources and keys each one expects, and point it at an export first rather than a live inbox.
Pair a detection skill with a writing skill. A risk list is only useful once someone sends the outreach, so pick a win-back or email skill that accepts the account research the detector produces.

topics.name: Sales
topics.name_re: \bsales\b|prospect|lead (?:gen|discovery|finder|enrichment|research|qualification|triage)|\bleads?\b|outreach|cold email|battle ?cards?|outbound|\bdeals?\b|account planning|enrichment|email finder|find email|verify email|contact finder|\bicp\b|\btam builder|signals?\b|predictable revenue|win back|demo builder|selling
topics.intro: Sales skills give an agent a full outbound and pipeline toolkit: ICP definition, prospect and lead list building, contact enrichment and email finding, buying signal detection, cold email sequences, battle cards and sales enablement collateral. Many connect to data providers such as Apollo, ContactOut, Hunter or Firecrawl, so the agent works from real company and contact records.
guide: Decide whether you need research, data or writing. Playbook skills (cold email frameworks, sales enablement, Predictable Revenue, forward deployed selling) are Markdown and need no keys; enrichment and email finder skills call a paid data provider and list its API key under Before you install.

Large collections such as the Gooseworks set split prospecting into many small skills: signal detection, enrichment, qualification, sequencing. Install the orchestrator or lead discovery skill with the pieces it calls, so hand-offs between steps work without extra prompting.

Check deliverability and consent rules before sending. Sequencing skills that set up Smartlead or other senders act on a real mailbox, so run them against a test domain and keep a human approval step before the first send.

topics.name: CRM
topics.intro: CRM skills connect an agent to the system of record for leads and deals: GoHighLevel accounts through an MCP server, Salesforce development and Flow design, deal logging to a Google Sheets tracker, contact databases and RevOps lifecycle design. They keep pipeline data clean and current while the agent works.
guide: Pick by the CRM you run. The GoHighLevel skill works through the NotFair MCP server, the Salesforce skills cover Apex, Lightning Web Components and Flow for developers, and the Google Workspace recipe writes deal updates to a sheet with no CRM at all.
RevOps skills define lifecycle stages, scoring, routing and handoff rules. Use them to design the process first, then apply it with the CRM-specific skill for your platform.
Any skill that writes to a CRM changes shared records. Start with a sandbox org or a test sub-account, and check the tool permissions listed on each page before you grant write access.

topics.name: Finance and Accounting
topics.intro: Finance and accounting skills cover budgets and expense tracking, SaaS revenue and unit economics, cloud cost management on AWS, Azure and GCP, FinOps investigations, SR&ED tax credit filings, portfolio optimization and crypto market data. They give an agent the formulas, data sources and review steps money questions need.
guide: Match the skill to the money you are tracking. SaaS metric and pricing skills are Markdown references with formulas and benchmarks; cloud cost skills query AWS, Azure, GKE billing or the hosted Costory MCP; budget skills build Excel or Google Sheets workbooks you own.

Market data and crypto skills call live APIs such as CoinPaprika, Octav or EmblemVault, and some can sign transactions. Read the Before you install panel for keys and tool permissions, and keep wallet skills in review-first mode until you trust them.
Keep a qualified reviewer on anything that files, pays or trades. These skills structure the analysis and the numbers; the decision and the signature stay with you.

topics.name: Legal
topics.name_re: legal|\bnda\b|\bgdpr\b|privacy policy|terms of service|compliance|contract review|iso standards
topics.intro: Legal skills help an agent draft and check the documents and controls that keep a business compliant: NDAs, privacy policies, GDPR engineering practices, API compliance patterns for PCI-DSS, SOC 2 and HIPAA, and ISO standards readiness evidence. They produce structured drafts and checklists a lawyer or compliance lead can review quickly.
guide: Use drafting skills for a first version. The NDA and privacy policy skills ask for parties, jurisdiction and data types, then produce a full draft with the clauses that need a decision marked for review.

Engineering compliance skills such as the GDPR and API compliance checkers work on your codebase. They are most useful during design and code review, when a data flow or log schema is still cheap to change.
Standards readiness skills organize evidence against named frameworks such as ISO 13485 and ISO 14971. Give them your actual procedures and records, and use their gap list to plan the audit.

guide: Candidate skills mostly come as a set: resume tailoring, bullet rewriting, ATS checks, cover letters, interview prep and offer comparison. Install the set and keep one master resume as the input every skill reads.

Job search and application skills browse job boards and fill Greenhouse, Lever or Workday forms. Check the tool permissions on each page, and review every answer before a form is submitted.

topics.name: E-commerce
topics.intro: E-commerce skills help an agent run and grow an online store: Shopify theme and app development, Stripe payments and integrations, Amazon listing checks and Amazon Ads, ecommerce SEO audits, product photo packshots, marketplace search and D2C business reviews from order data.
guide: Platform skills come from the vendors and track their current APIs. The Stripe set covers integration choices, Connect, payments and SDK upgrades; use test-mode keys first, and check the Official tag on each page.

Growth skills split by channel. Ecommerce SEO skills audit category and product pages, Amazon skills cover listing copy and ACoS-aware ads, and the D2C review skill runs a bundled Python engine over your order CSVs.
Creative skills such as product packshots and reels call hosted image or video models. They read an API key shown under Before you install, and usage is billed by that provider.

guide: Use canvas and strategy skills early. Lean canvas, startup canvas and beachhead skills are Markdown frameworks that turn a raw idea into a one-page plan you can test.

Fundraising skills research investors and prepare calls. Some pull meetings from Google Calendar and enrich investor profiles with paid data sources, so check the variables listed under Before you install.

topics.name: Real Estate
topics.intro: Real estate skills help an agent with property listings, market comparisons, rental analysis and client communication for agents, investors and property managers. This topic collects listings as publishers add skills built for real estate work.
guide: Look for skills that work from listing data you can export, such as MLS or portal CSVs, so the agent analyzes your actual inventory.
Market and valuation skills often call a property data API. Check the Before you install panel for the key each one reads and the terms of that data source.
Use the listing request link on this page to ask for a real estate skill, or submit one you have built for the directory.

topics.name: Presentations
topics.intro: Presentation skills let an agent build and edit slide decks in every common format: PowerPoint files with python-pptx and PptxGenJS, Google Slides through the API, animated HTML decks, React and Chart.js slides, scientific talks and posters, with layout, palette and speaker notes handled.
guide: Choose by the file your audience opens. PPTX skills produce editable PowerPoint files, Google Slides skills write to a Drive account, and HTML deck skills produce a web page you present from a browser.

Several collections split deck work into planning, design system and single-slide steps. MiniMax ships an orchestration skill plus editing and slide-making skills; install them together so each step hands off cleanly.
Check the license on each page. The Anthropic document skills use proprietary terms that restrict copying, and the directory shows that in place of install commands.

topics.name: Spreadsheets
topics.intro: Spreadsheet skills let an agent open, build and edit Excel and Google Sheets files: formulas and recalculation, formatting and charts, CSV conversion, tab comparison, monthly template copies, budget and expense trackers, and reports generated from sheet data.
guide: Local file skills (xlsx, MiniMax xlsx, convert to Markdown) work on files on disk with bundled Python scripts. Google Sheets skills read and write through the Workspace API and need an authorized account.

For recurring work, the Google Workspace recipes are small, single-purpose skills: back up a sheet as CSV, copy a tab for a new month, create calendar events from rows. Install only the recipes you use.
Ask the agent to recalculate and reopen the workbook it produced. Skills that validate formulas catch broken references before you share the file.

topics.name: Note Taking
topics.intro: Note taking skills give an agent a place to keep what it learns: Notion knowledge capture, meeting intelligence and research pages, NotebookLM and Open Notebook queries, Outline wikis, LLM-curated Markdown wikis, local knowledge vaults, brain dump capture and session logs.
guide: Pick the home for your notes first. Notion skills need the Notion MCP server or API token, NotebookLM skills use a browser profile login, and Markdown wiki and vault skills write plain files to a folder you control.
Notion has two parallel collections, from Notion and from OpenAI, covering the same jobs. Install one set so your agent has a single way to capture and search pages.
Capture skills work best on a routine. Run session logs and knowledge capture at the end of each working session, so notes stay complete without a separate cleanup pass.

topics.name: Personal Assistant

topics.intro: Personal assistant skills let an agent handle the daily admin around your work: executive inbox and schedule management, daily prep and status briefings, Google Workspace cross-service workflows, Microsoft 365 data through WorkIQ, restaurant booking, shopping research, weather and SMS messages.
guide: Most assistant skills act on your accounts. Google Workspace skills use the gws CLI with OAuth, WorkIQ uses its CLI or MCP server for Microsoft 365, and SMS sends through a Textbelt key, all listed under Before you install.
Briefing skills such as daily prep and roundup read several sources and produce one summary. Configure their data sources once and run them on a schedule.
Keep send and book actions behind your approval. Skills that book tables or send texts act in the real world, so review the draft before the agent completes it.

topics.name: Scheduling and Calendar
topics.name_re: calendar|schedul|free time|focus time|booking|appointment|event coordinator|invite to event
topics.intro: Scheduling skills let an agent manage calendars: Google Calendar event creation, updates and deletion, free and busy lookups to find a meeting slot, recurring events, focus time blocks, rescheduling with attendee notices, weekly schedule planning and events created from spreadsheet rows.
guide: Almost every scheduling skill works through Google Calendar, either with the gws CLI or the Calendar API, so authorize one Google account and use it across the set.
The Google Workspace recipes are single tasks (find free time, block focus time, reschedule a meeting). Install the ones you repeat each week, and use the full calendar skill for anything else.
Changes notify attendees. Ask the agent to show the event before it saves, especially for recurring events and reschedules.

topics.name: Meeting Assistant
topics.intro: Meeting assistant skills cover the full meeting cycle for an agent: agendas and private prep briefs, attendee research, Google Meet spaces and participant reviews, minutes and structured notes from transcripts, recaps with decisions and actions, and synthesis across many past meetings.
guide: Split prep from follow-up. Prep skills read your calendar and research attendees, sometimes with paid enrichment sources; follow-up skills work from a transcript or notes you supply and need no account access.
The pm-skills meeting set (agenda, brief, recap, synthesize) shares one format, so recaps feed the synthesis skill cleanly. Install the four together if you run many recurring meetings.
Notion meeting intelligence skills pull context from your workspace into pre-reads. They need the Notion connection set up, which the Before you install panel notes.

topics.intro: Task management skills help an agent turn work into tracked action: brain dump capture, Google Tasks lists and overdue reviews, email to task conversion, team goals and milestones, Pomodoro focus sessions, a daily focus board and prioritized action plans that unblock stuck items.
guide: Choose where tasks live. Google Tasks skills need Workspace access through the gws CLI, team goal skills write to the Hivemind Deeplake filesystem, and capture and action plan skills produce Markdown you can paste anywhere.

Keep one system of record. Use these skills to feed the tracker you already check every day, rather than starting a second list the agent maintains alone.

guide: Pick by source. URL and article skills fetch and clean pages, video skills pull transcripts or keyframes, and interview and meeting skills work from a transcript you paste in.
Some summarizers call an external tool or API, such as the summarize CLI or a transcript service. The Before you install panel lists any key or binary they need.
Ask for the summary format you will use. Skills that output decisions, action items or quotes with timestamps are easier to verify than a free-form paragraph.

topics.name: Translation and Localization
topics.intro: Translation and localization skills help an agent publish in more than one language: blog post translation and cultural adaptation, multilingual blog creation, hreflang audits for international SEO, Flutter and VS Code extension localization, MkDocs translations and localization-ready interface design.
guide: Separate content translation from software localization. Blog translation skills rewrite prose for each market; Flutter, VS Code and MkDocs skills set up the string files and tooling a codebase needs.
For international sites, pair a translation skill with an hreflang audit skill so every language version is linked and indexed correctly.
Have a fluent reviewer check each language before publishing. Localization skills adjust examples and calls to action, and a native reader confirms tone.

guide: Each search skill wraps one provider and reads that provider's API key, shown under Before you install. Pick the provider you already pay for, or one with a free tier for testing.
Choose by result type. SERP skills return ranked links and metadata, neural and research skills return extracted page content, and deep research modes return a cited report.
Install one primary search skill so the agent uses it consistently. Add a second only for a specific need, such as scholarly results or shopping data.

topics.name: Prompt Generators
topics.intro: Prompt generator skills write and improve prompts for you: system prompts for any model, prompt optimization from trace data, refinement workflows, prompt testing, image and video prompts for Replicate and fal.ai, UI prompts for Stitch and goal commands for Claude Code and Codex.
guide: Split model prompts from media prompts. System prompt and optimizer skills target LLM agents; Replicate, fal.ai and Vibe Creating skills teach the prompt patterns that image and video models respond to.
Optimization skills that use production traces, such as the Arize skill, need access to that platform. The Before you install panel lists the variables they read.
Test before you adopt. Run a rewritten prompt and the original on the same inputs, and keep the version that produces better results on your own cases.

topics.name: Chatbots
topics.intro: Chatbot skills help an agent create and train conversational bots on your content: websites, sitemaps, articles and documents, published through a hosted service. This topic lists skills built specifically for chatbot creation.
guide: Hosted chatbot skills such as Appie create and train bots through the provider's MCP server. Set up the server and key listed under Before you install.
Train on content you own and keep current. A chatbot answers from its sources, so schedule retraining when your docs change.
Use the listing request link on this page to ask for more chatbot skills, or submit one for the directory.

topics.name: PDF
topics.intro: PDF skills cover every common PDF job: text and table extraction, merging and splitting, form filling, watermarking and redaction, OCR, creating designed PDFs from scratch or from Markdown, natural-language edits and conversion to Markdown for analysis.
guide: Local skills (pdf, pdftk, make-pdf, nano-pdf) run bundled scripts or a command-line tool on your machine. Install the tool each one names, such as pdftk or the nano-pdf CLI.
Nutrient handles OCR, redaction and signing through its hosted processor and reads an API key. Use it when you need those operations at production quality.
Ask the agent to render and check the PDF it produced. Skills that compare the visual output catch layout problems that text extraction misses.

topics.intro: SEO skills give your agent a working search practice: full-site and single-page audits, technical crawls, schema markup, hreflang, sitemaps, backlinks, local SEO and keyword clustering. guide: Start with scope. Collections such as claude-seo and NotFair split the job into narrow skills (seo-page for one URL, seo-technical for crawlability, seo-local for Google Business Profile), so install the router skill plus the few lanes you actually run.

Check the data source before you install. Procedure-only audits need nothing but the page.

Prefer skills that end in a scored, prioritized report or a ready-to-paste fix (JSON-LD, a sitemap, a meta tag set). Those outputs are easy to review and hand to a developer, and they make before-and-after comparisons simple when you rerun the audit.

topics.name: AI Search Visibility
topics.text_re: generative engine optimi|answer engine optimi|\bgeo\b|\baeo\b|ai overviews|ai citations?|cited by (?:llms|ai)|llms\.txt|ai search
topics.intro: These skills work on how a brand shows up in AI answers: Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT search, Perplexity, Copilot and Claude. They audit citation readiness, entity clarity and AI crawler access, check llms.txt, rewrite content so answer engines can quote it, and track share of citations over time.
guide: Separate fixing from measuring. Optimizer skills (geo-optimizer, seo-geo, blog-geo) rewrite and restructure pages; tracker skills (seo-profound, seo-seranking, aeo) report how often AI engines cite you and read from the tracking service behind them.

Look at what each skill checks on the technical side. Some probe robots.txt rules for GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot and validate llms.txt with plain curl calls; others focus on page copy, schema and entity consistency. A full program usually wants one of each.

Pair this topic with an SEO audit skill from the same collection. AI answer engines lean on the same crawlable, well-structured pages that rank in classic search, so a shared vocabulary between the two skills keeps the fix list in one place.

topics.name: Email
topics.intro: Email skills cover the whole channel: lifecycle and drip sequences, cold outbound, personal drafting, inbox triage, and the sending infrastructure underneath (Resend, Mailtrap, Amazon SES, Cloudflare). They help an agent write the message, wire the template, and keep deliverability rules such as SPF, DKIM and DMARC in view.
guide: Decide which layer you need. Copy skills (emails, cold-email, email-drafter) produce sequences and drafts; developer skills (react-email, resend, sending-emails) build templates and send through an API; Gmail and Google Workspace recipes act on a real inbox.

Check credentials up front. Resend, Mailtrap, SES and Smartlead skills need that provider's API key, and the Gmail and gws recipes need an authorized Google account. Drafting and sequence-planning skills run on the brief you give them.

For outbound, pick a skill that treats deliverability and consent as part of the job: bounded follow-up counts, unsubscribe handling, and current Gmail and Yahoo sender rules. Review every send step yourself before a campaign goes live.

topics.name: Social Media
topics.name_re: social|linkedin|twitter|\bx post|\bx content|tiktok|instagram|reddit|outlier post|comment mining|creator profile|trend discovery
topics.intro: Social media skills plan, write and research organic posts for LinkedIn, X, Instagram, TikTok and Reddit. Matches include post writers with hook libraries, content calendars, repurposing from blogs and video, social listening, outlier-post analysis, and short vertical reels built from product pages or audio.
guide: Match the skill to the platform. The linkedin-skills collection covers posts, comments, replies, profiles and employee advocacy in depth; goose-skills splits drafting (create-x-content, create-linkedin-content) from research (social-listening, trend-discovery, outlier-post-finder).

Research skills that read live profiles, search TikTok or monitor mentions call third-party scrapers or APIs and list the key they need. Writing skills work from a brief and, in several cases, a voice guide you generate once and reuse.

Keep publishing in your own hands. Schedulers such as timetopost-social-scheduler stop for approval of the exact post and time, which is the pattern to look for in any skill that touches a live account.

topics.name: Advertising
topics.name_re: \bads?\b|advertis|paid media|\bppc\b|google ads|meta ads|headline matrix|scroll stopping creative|ad angle
topics.intro: Advertising skills run paid media for an agent: Google Ads, Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok, X, Reddit and Amazon campaigns, from account audits and search term cleanup to ad copy, creative angles, policy checks and landing page message match. Several operate a connected ad account; others work entirely from exported data and briefs.
guide: Know whether a skill reads or writes. The NotFair paid-ads skills and google-ads operate connected accounts through the NotFair MCP; Google Ads API skills walk you through developer token and OAuth setup; creative skills such as ad-creative and headline-matrix only need your product facts.

For performance questions, start with a read-only review (paid-ads-review, ad-campaign-analyzer, meta-ads-analyzer) on an export before you let any skill change bids or budgets. Look for skills that pause new campaigns by default and state spend changes before making them.

For creative, prefer skills that check platform character limits and ad policy, and that ground every claim in a source you supplied. That keeps rejected ads and unsupported promises out of the account.

topics.name: Content Marketing
topics.intro: Content marketing skills decide what to publish and turn that decision into briefs, calendars and repurposed assets. Matches include content strategy frameworks, SERP-based content briefs, topic cluster maps, editorial calendars driven by Search Console data, site content inventories, and customer story builders.
guide: Separate planning from production. Strategy and cluster skills (content-strategy, topic-cluster-planning, topical-authority-mapper) produce a map; brief skills (content-brief, seo-content-brief, content-brief-factory) produce writer-ready instructions for one piece at a time.

Check the inputs each brief skill needs. Some read the live top ten results for a keyword through a search or scraping service; content-planner works from your Search Console data; strategy skills work from the audience and product context you supply.
Choose skills that tie every recommendation to a KPI or a search query. A calendar that names the query each piece targets is far easier to measure and prune than a list of topic ideas.

topics.name: Marketing Analytics
topics.name_re: analytics|attribution|conversion tracking|\bga4\b|google analytics|growth report|matomo|ab testing|a b testing|messaging ab|event ingestion|performance diagnosis
topics.intro: Marketing analytics skills set up and read the numbers behind campaigns: GA4 and Tag Manager tracking plans, conversion and server-side event ingestion, attribution models, A/B test design and readouts, and SEO performance reports. They help an agent prove what fired and which channel moved revenue.
guide: Pick by question. Tracking skills (analytics, suede-analytics) build the event plan; attribution skills explain why dashboards disagree; ab-testing and suede-ab-testing handle sample size, duration and significance; Google Analytics API skills manage properties and pull reports.

API skills need a Google Cloud project and Analytics access, and the Data Manager API skills need a Google Cloud project with that API enabled. Planning and readout skills work from exports you paste in.

Favor skills that verify instrumentation by reading back what actually fires rather than trusting the tag configuration. A tracking plan is only useful once every key event shows up in the report it feeds.

topics.name: Lead Generation
topics.name_re: lead gen|lead magnets?|lead quality|scorecard marketing|free tools|popups?|signup
topics.text_re: lead generation|lead magnets?|lead capture|qualified leads|email capture|opt-?ins?
topics.intro: Lead generation skills build the assets and flows that turn visitors into contacts: lead magnets, free tools and calculators, quiz and scorecard funnels, popups, signup flows, and prospect discovery. A few go further and measure true cost per qualified lead from paid campaigns.
guide: Decide between inbound and outbound. Inbound skills (lead-magnets, free-tools, scorecard-marketing, popups, signup) shape what you offer on your own site; prospecting skills (lead-discovery, firecrawl-lead-gen) find people and companies to contact and need that data provider's key.
Ask each skill how it qualifies a lead. The stronger ones define the qualifying signal up front and connect the asset to a paid offer, which keeps a list from filling with contacts who never buy.
Pair this topic with an email skill. A lead magnet or free tool only pays off when the follow-up sequence is ready on the day it launches.

topics.name: Influencer Marketing
topics.intro: Influencer marketing skills find, vet and pitch creators. Matches evaluate audience fit and authenticity from public profiles, tear down a creator's content strategy, search X for relevant voices, draft first-touch outreach, and plan UGC-style creator ads.
guide: Vet before you pitch. audience-research and influencer-prospecting score audience fit and authenticity from public data; creator-profile-teardown explains what a creator's best posts have in common.

Profile lookups and searches call third-party scrapers, so check the key each skill lists. Outreach skills such as suede-influencer-outreach work from your offer and the creator's public work and leave sending to you.
For paid creator content, the ugc skill plans direct-to-camera ads and generates them through fal.ai media models, which requires a fal API key and usage billing on that account.

topics.name: Affiliate and Referral Programs
topics.intro: These skills design programs where customers, affiliates and partners bring in new buyers: referral incentives, affiliate commission and payout rules, fraud controls, co-marketing partner selection, and word-of-mouth campaigns built on the STEPPS framework.
guide: Use referrals and suede-referrals for program mechanics: who earns what, when payouts happen, how disclosure works, and which fraud patterns to block. Use co-marketing skills when the partner is another company rather than an individual.
Check that the program design names its measurement. A referral program needs a tracked link or code and a reporting view on day one, so pair it with a marketing analytics skill.
These skills are procedure and need no credentials. Your referral or affiliate platform and payment provider handle the live program.

topics.name: Branding
topics.text_re: brand voice|brand guidelines|brand identity|brand kit|positioning|naming|brand messaging
topics.intro: Branding skills define and apply what a brand is: positioning statements, product and company naming, brand voice extraction, brand kits with logos, colors and fonts, StoryBrand messaging, value propositions, and brand consistency checks on screens and copy.
guide: Strategy first, assets second. Positioning and naming skills (obviously-awesome, positioning-statement, naming, product-name) produce decisions; brand kit and asset skills (update-brand-kit, get-brand-assets, visual-brand-extractor) package those decisions for other skills to read.
Asset lookup skills pull logos, colors and fonts from a domain through services such as Brand.dev and list the key they need. Voice extraction skills read your published pages and need only the URLs.

Keep one brand file as the source of truth. Several of these skills write a durable BRAND or brand kit document that copy, ad and social skills read later, which keeps every downstream draft on the same voice.

topics.name: Landing Pages and Conversion
topics.name_re: landing page|\bcro\b|conversion (?:optimi|path|methodology)|site alchemy|improve website|grow website|create website|paywalls?|icp website
topics.intro: These skills audit and improve the pages where conversions happen: landing pages, signup and checkout flows, paywalls and upgrade screens. Matches score pages for conversion leaks, check message match between an ad and its landing page, design funnels from click to booked call, and plan evidence-based tests.
guide: Audit skills (landing-page-conversion-audit, landing-page-auditor, cro-methodology) return an ordered fix list; journey skills (improve-website, grow-website, create-website) orchestrate several skills across research, copy and design.
Most of these skills work from a URL or pasted page and need no credentials. Ad-to-page skills read your ad copy, and paywall skills work best with your current pricing and plan limits in hand.
Pair a conversion audit with an A/B testing or analytics skill so every recommended change ships with a way to measure it.

topics.name: Product Descriptions
topics.name_re: product descri|listing checker|ecommerce seo|seo ecommerce|\baso\b|app store optimi
topics.intro: These skills write and check the copy that sells a product on a listing page: Amazon listing review, App Store and Google Play optimization, ecommerce product page SEO and product schema. They keep titles, bullets and keyword fields inside each marketplace's limits.
guide: Choose by storefront. amazon-listing-checker reviews pasted Amazon copy with a local Python script; aso and suede-aso cover App Store and Google Play fields; seo-ecommerce and ecommerce-seo audit product and category pages on your own store.
Marketplace analysis that pulls live Shopping or Amazon data uses a data provider such as DataForSEO, so check the key the skill lists. Copy review skills run on the text you paste.
For new product copy from scratch, pair a listing skill with a copywriting skill. The listing skill enforces structure and limits; the copywriting skill supplies the angle and proof.

topics.name: Marketing Automation
topics.name_re: marketing loops?|lifecycle messaging|\bsms\b|campaign orchestrat|full funnel|marketing automation
topics.intro: Marketing automation skills set up campaigns and workflows that run on their own: email lifecycle flows, consent-aware SMS and MMS programs, recurring marketing loops an agent runs on a schedule, and orchestrators that coordinate a full-funnel campaign across several skills.
guide: Lifecycle skills (emails, suede-emails, lifecycle-messaging) design triggered sequences; SMS skills cover welcome, cart recovery and win-back flows with consent and quiet-hours rules; marketing-loops and suede-marketing-loops define a repeatable loop with cadence, conditions and stored state.
These skills design the automation; your email service, SMS provider or scheduler runs it. Check each flow's consent and opt-out handling before it goes live.
Start small. Automate one loop with a clear trigger and success metric, review its first runs by hand, then add the next.

topics.name: Marketing Strategy
topics.name_re: marketing (?:plan|ideas|council|psychology)|gtm|go to market|one page marketing|launch|crossing the chasm|growth loops|product marketing|campaign brief
topics.text_re: marketing plan|go-to-market|gtm strateg|product launch|launch plan|marketing strateg
topics.intro: Marketing strategy skills turn a product and a goal into a plan: go-to-market motions, launch plans and checklists, marketing plans with tactic shortlists, positioning for new categories, growth loops, product-led growth, and simulated advisory councils that pressure-test a contested decision.
guide: For a full plan, start with marketing-plan, suede-marketing-plan or one-page-marketing. For a launch, use launch or gtm-0-to-1-launch plus a checklist skill. For a single hard call, a council skill gives several expert perspectives in one pass.

These are reasoning skills and need no credentials. Their output is only as good as the product marketing context you give them, so keep a current positioning and ICP document and point each skill at it.
Prefer skills that end with a prioritized shortlist and a 30, 60 or 90 day schedule over open-ended idea lists. A ranked plan with owners is the part you can act on.

topics.name: Copywriting
topics.name_re: copywrit|copy editing|\bcopy\b|headline|ogilvy|ux writing|made to stick|generic language
topics.intro: Copywriting skills write and edit persuasive copy: landing and homepage copy, headlines, ad copy, UI microcopy and CTAs. Matches include classic frameworks (Ogilvy, Made to Stick), headline matrices, copy editing passes, and plain-language filters that strip vague corporate wording.
guide: Use a writing skill to draft and an editing skill to tighten. copywriting and suede-copy produce page copy; copy-editing, generic-language-killer and ogilvy-copywriting review and sharpen what you already have.
Give each skill real inputs: product facts, customer language, proof you can cite, and the offer. Skills that ask for these before drafting produce copy you can publish with fewer rewrites.
For ads, choose a skill that checks platform character limits (google-ads-copy, ad-creative). For product interfaces, ux-writing covers error messages, empty states and button labels.

topics.name: Rewriting and Paraphrasing
topics.intro: Rewriting skills take text you already have and return a better version: voice-preserving rewrites, ghostwritten messages and docs, AI-pattern cleanup, blog refreshes for current search guidelines, and rewrites of commit messages and review comments so they read like a teammate wrote them.
guide: Decide what must stay fixed. voice-preserving-rewriter and file-edit-in-place protect your facts, code, links and formatting while they rewrite; ghostwriter writes in a stored voice for you or your company.
For published pages, blog-rewrite and suede-copy rewrite toward a goal (rankings, AI citations, conversion) rather than style alone. Supply the target keyword or the page goal with the text.
These skills are plain Markdown procedure with no credentials. Ask for a diff or a change list so you can accept edits one by one.

topics.name: Storytelling and Fiction
topics.name_re: story|fiction|novel|chapter|plot|worldbuilding|character management|scene craft|premise|genre craft|theme craft|verse|poem|reader panel|discovery drafting
topics.intro: Storytelling skills support long-form creative writing: premise workshops, plot structure, characters, worldbuilding, scene craft, chapter drafting, poetry, interactive fiction, beta-reader simulation and continuity checks across a series. A few extend into multi-shot narrative image and video work.
guide: Collections such as story-skills keep a story project on disk (characters, timeline, chapters), so install the init skill first and let the others read and update the same files.
Single-skill options such as fiction-studio and novel-writing guide one manuscript from idea to draft in one place. They suit a writer who wants a guided path over a toolkit of separate steps.
These skills need no credentials. The multi-shot storytelling skill in the media category generates images, video and audio through a hosted model service and needs that service's key.

topics.name: Grammar and Proofreading
topics.name_re: grammar|proofread|line editing|copy editing|writing guidelines|style guide|em dash
topics.intro: Grammar and proofreading skills check text against rules and return targeted fixes: grammar, logic and flow errors, line-level copyediting, house style sheets, correct punctuation, and documentation writing guidelines. They fix what is wrong without rewriting your whole draft.
guide: grammar-check suits short business text where you want minimal changes; line-editing suits fiction and long-form prose; writing-guidelines and voice-style enforce a written style guide you already have.
Ask for changes with reasons. Every skill here can return a list of edits instead of a rewritten file, which keeps your voice intact and makes review quick.
These skills are plain Markdown and need no credentials or network access.

topics.name: AI Detection and Humanizing
topics.name_re: humani[sz]|slop|deslop|ai writing|false positive reviewer|voice checker|preservation verifier|voice preserving
topics.intro: These skills find and remove the patterns that make text read as machine-written: stock vocabulary, stacked hedges, tricolons, formulaic openers and closers. Matches include detectors that score text without changing it, voice-preserving rewriters, language-specific humanizers for Finnish and Russian, and LinkedIn-specific cleanup.
guide: Separate detection from rewriting. ai-writing-detector and false-positive-reviewer score and explain flags without touching your text; avoid-ai-writing, unslop, stop-slop and suede-deslop rewrite it.

Check how a rewriter protects content. The stronger skills preserve code, quotes, links, frontmatter and facts and verify that afterward; HumanPen rewrites .docx and .pptx files through its hosted service, which needs an account.
No detector proves authorship. Use these skills to improve clarity and voice, and read flagged passages yourself before changing them.

topics.name: General Writing
topics.name_re: ghostwriter|prose style|internal comms|write$|writing guide|doc coauthoring|eli5|ship copy
topics.text_re: writes?,? rewrites?|writing style|in the user'?s voice|prose
topics.intro: General writing skills give an agent a house standard for everyday prose: internal communications, co-authored docs and proposals, ghostwritten messages, plain explanations, and reusable style contracts for reports and agent output.
guide: Pick a skill whose default format matches your work. internal-comms covers status updates and newsletters in a company format; doc-coauthoring runs a structured drafting workflow for proposals and specs; eli5 picks the clearest form for an explanation.
Style contracts such as prose-style and writing-guidelines are most useful installed once and applied everywhere, so every draft your agent writes follows the same rules.
These skills are plain Markdown and need no credentials. Read the standard in the SKILL.md before you install it; it is the whole product.

topics.name: Resumes and Cover Letters
topics.intro: Resume skills help a job seeker write and tailor application materials: ATS-friendly resumes, achievement-focused bullets with metrics, executive and academic CVs, cover letters for a specific posting, and resume reviews against a job description.
guide: Tailoring skills (resume-tailor, resume-ats-optimizer, cover-letter) work best with the exact job posting pasted in; writing skills (resume-bullet-writer, resume-quantifier) work from your raw experience notes.
Keep a master resume and let resume-version-manager track the tailored copies. That makes it easy to see which version went to which employer.
These skills need no credentials. Check every metric they suggest against what you actually did before you send anything.

topics.name: Essays and Academic Writing
topics.name_re: essay|scientific writing|academic writ|paper writing|research grants|literature review|peer review|\bthesis\b|dissertation
topics.intro: Academic writing skills draft and review scholarly work: scientific manuscripts with reporting-guideline checks, ML and systems conference papers, systematic literature reviews, structured peer reviews, and research grant proposals.
guide: Match the skill to the venue. ml-paper-writing targets NeurIPS, ICML and ACL style papers; systems-paper-writing targets OSDI and SOSP; research-grants covers NSF, NIH and DOE proposals.
Literature review skills search scholarly databases such as PubMed and need network access; some sources require an API key. Drafting and peer-review skills work from the material you provide.
Keep sources traceable. Prefer skills that record where each claim came from, and verify every citation yourself before submission.

topics.name: Blog Writing
topics.intro: Blog skills cover a post from plan to publish: outlines from SERP research, full drafts optimized for search and AI citations, fact-checks of statistics against their sources, voice and persona setup, schema, taxonomy, cannibalization checks and repurposing into social posts.
guide: The claude-blog family in dev-gtm-claude-skills splits the job into many lanes behind one router; install the router and the lanes you use. Single-skill options such as write-content, content-writer and make-blog-post produce a full article in one pass.
Hosted options such as appie-article-writer and timetopost-autoseo-blog draft through their service and need that account's API key. Local skills work from your brief and any research they fetch.
Run a fact-check pass before publishing. blog-factcheck fetches cited sources and checks that each number actually appears there.

topics.name: Scriptwriting
topics.intro: Scriptwriting skills write words meant to be performed: short-form video ad scripts built from a sourced angle, screenplays and audiobook narration adapted from existing stories, and YouTube scripts repurposed from blog posts.
guide: write-video-ad-script plans words, product proof and shots for a short ad; adaptation converts a story into screenplay (Fountain), audio narration or picture-book formats; blog-repurpose turns a post into a script among other formats.
These skills need no credentials. Pair a script with a video or voice skill when you want the agent to produce the finished asset.
Read scripts aloud before recording. Timing that looks right on the page often runs long once spoken.

topics.name: Books and Publishing
topics.name_re: publishing|submission|novel writing|fiction studio|series continuity|feedback triage|editorial review
topics.intro: Book skills take a manuscript from draft to market: novel planning and drafting, series continuity, editorial and sensitivity review, beta-reader feedback triage, query letters and synopses for agents, and self-publishing setup covering ISBNs, metadata, BISAC codes, KDP and IngramSpark.
guide: Use drafting skills (fiction-studio, novel-writing) while the book is being written, review skills (editorial-review, feedback-triage) once a draft exists, and submission or publishing skills at the end.
For traditional publishing, submission writes query letters, synopses and blurbs; for self-publishing, publishing walks through ISBNs, copyright pages and retailer metadata.
These skills are procedure and need no credentials. Retailer accounts and ISBN purchases happen outside the agent.

topics.name: Technical Writing and Documentation
topics.intro: Technical writing skills produce and audit developer documentation: Diataxis-structured docs, API and SDK references, docstrings and language doc comments for Go, Dart, C# and Java, READMEs, release notes and changelogs, plus scored audits of an entire docs site.
guide: Writers and auditors are separate. diataxis-writer, documentation, code-documenter and api-documentation write docs; docs-auditor, api-docs-quality-report and sdk-docs-auditor crawl a published site and score it.

Language skills (go-documentation, dart-write-documentation, csharp-docs, java-docs) follow one ecosystem's conventions, so install the one that matches your codebase. Release note skills work from tickets, PRDs or git history.
Most of these skills are plain Markdown with no credentials. Site auditors fetch pages over the network and some produce an HTML report you can share with the docs owner.

topics.name: Code Assistants
topics.name_re: refactor(?!ing ui)|\bcoding agent|\bcode ?gen|pair program|quasi coder|^implement(?: spec)?\b|code transfer|karpathy guidelines|tiny stepping|grok build
topics.intro: Skills that shape how an agent writes and changes code: refactoring playbooks, spec-to-implementation workflows, small-step development and handoffs to other coding agents such as Jules or Grok Build. They give the agent a working method so edits stay deliberate across a large codebase.
guide: Separate method skills from delegation skills. Refactoring and implementation workflows run inside your own agent as Markdown instructions; delegation skills hand work to another coding agent and need that agent's CLI or account set up first.

Refactoring skills range from single named moves (extract method, remove parameter) to multi-file plans. Pick the narrow ones for routine cleanup and the planning ones before a change that touches many files.

Workflow skills like tiny stepping or implement-from-spec change how the agent approaches every task. Install one method and keep it, since overlapping methods give the agent conflicting instructions.

topics.name: SQL and Databases
topics.intro: Skills for writing queries, designing schemas and running databases, from PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server to Redis, Qdrant, Neon and Supabase. Many come from the database vendors, so the agent follows the engine's own conventions for indexing, migrations and scaling.
guide: Start with the engine you run. Vendor collections from Redis, Qdrant, Neon, Supabase and AWS encode dialect details and limits that general SQL skills miss.
Check whether a skill connects to a live database. Query runners for Postgres, MySQL and SQL Server read connection settings from environment variables; give them a read-only role first.
For migrations, such as Oracle to PostgreSQL, install the whole set from one collection. Those skills hand plans, code changes and test projects to each other in sequence.

topics.name: Low-Code and No-Code
topics.intro: Skills that build and govern Microsoft Power Platform work: Power Apps code apps, Power Automate cloud flows and custom connectors. They let an agent scaffold, debug and monitor low-code solutions the way a platform team would.
guide: Most of these skills work through the FlowStudio MCP server or the PAC CLI. Read SKILL.md for the server or CLI to install and the tenant permissions it needs.
Monitoring and governance skills operate across a whole tenant; one notes a Pro+ subscription requirement. Check those terms before you install.
Use the architect skill first when you are turning business requirements into a solution, then the build and debug skills once flows exist.

topics.name: App Builders
topics.name_re: ^create app\b|app builder|app factory|site to ios app|^angular new app|project bootstrapper|^scaffold nextjs|full ?stack|start building|app onboard|launch with aws|n tier serverless web app
topics.intro: Skills that take an app from idea to a running first version: guided app creation, project scaffolds for Next.js and Angular, full-stack starters and platform onboarding for AWS, Azure and Google Cloud. They give an agent a repeatable path from blank folder to deployable app.
guide: Decide whether you want a method or a platform. Guided skills such as create-app and design-code-architecture work with any stack; AWS Amplify, AWS Blocks, Azure and Google Cloud skills target that provider and need its CLI and account.
Scaffold skills encode a house toolchain. Read the generated stack in SKILL.md before you adopt it, since a scaffold is easiest to change on day one.
Mobile builders, such as the Android and site-to-iOS factories, need the platform SDKs installed locally. The Before you install panel lists the scripts each one runs.

topics.name: Website Builders
topics.text_re: (?:designs and )?builds? (?:complete )?(?:web experiences|websites?)\b|iteratively build websites|building a website
topics.intro: Skills that build whole websites with an agent: message-first site creation, cinematic landing pages and iterative builds in Google Stitch. They give the agent a sequence for structure, design and copy so a site comes out finished rather than templated.
guide: create-website works from your message outward and suits a new marketing site; Auteur focuses on high-craft landing pages and scroll-directed experiences.
Stitch skills need access to Google Stitch and run an iterative build loop there, so pick them when that is your design tool.
Pair a builder with a design skill from Frontend and Design if you want stricter visual rules across pages.

topics.name: CLIs and Terminal Tools
topics.name_re: cli developer|cli creator|scaffold cli|build cli app|^go cli\b|system commandline|command line|terminal|tmux
topics.intro: Skills for building command-line tools and working in the terminal: CLI design in Go, Dart, TypeScript and .NET, tools generated from API docs, tmux control for interactive programs and terminal recordings. They teach an agent flag handling, exit codes and stdout discipline.
guide: Pick the builder skill for your language. Go, Dart, TypeScript and System.CommandLine skills each follow that ecosystem's packaging and argument parsing conventions.
cli-creator turns API docs or an OpenAPI spec into a composable CLI, a quick route when you need agent-friendly access to a service.
Terminal workflow skills such as tmux control and terminal titles change how the agent runs commands. They are small Markdown skills and easy to try.

topics.name: Game Development
topics.intro: Skills for building games: Unity and Unreal systems, web game engines on HTML5 Canvas, Minecraft server plugins and generated 2D pixel art and sprite sheets. They give an agent the patterns a game team uses for loops, assets and performance.
guide: Match the engine. The Unity and Unreal skill, the web engine skill and the Minecraft plugin skill each target a different runtime and do not substitute for one another.
Asset generation through fal.ai calls a hosted model and reads an API key; usage is billed by that provider.
Engine work benefits from a run-and-check loop. Ask the agent to build and launch the game after changes rather than reviewing code alone.

topics.name: React and Next.js
topics.intro: Skills for React and Next.js work: App Router and server components, composition patterns, React 18 and 19 migrations, view transitions and performance rules from Vercel. They keep an agent on current React APIs instead of patterns from older tutorials.
guide: Check the React version each skill targets. The React 18 and 19 migration skills are written as before-and-after patterns for that upgrade, while best-practice skills assume a current release.
For Next.js, prefer skills written for the App Router if that is what you run; several cover server components and server actions directly.
Vercel's React skills are guidelines in Markdown and quick to adopt. Skills that deploy, such as Next.js on Cloudflare, need that platform's CLI and credentials.

topics.name: Vue and Nuxt
topics.intro: Skills for Vue 3 and Nuxt: Composition API components, Pinia stores, Nuxt SSR and SSG setup, Vite configuration and unit tests with Vitest. They give an agent the conventions of a modern Vue codebase.
guide: Choose between the TypeScript and plain JavaScript Vue skills based on your codebase; both cover components, routing and state.
Add the Vue and Pinia unit test skill when you want tests written in Vitest alongside new components.
These skills are Markdown guidance with no credentials, so they are safe to try on any Vue project.

topics.name: Angular
topics.intro: Skills for Angular applications, including official ones from the Angular team: signals, standalone components, forms, routing, server rendering, NgRx and new app setup with the Angular CLI. They keep an agent on current Angular APIs.
guide: Start with the Official Angular skills. They track the framework's current guidance on signals and standalone components.
Use angular-new-app for a fresh project and angular-developer for ongoing work; the community architect skill adds NgRx and lazy-loading patterns.
For end-to-end tests, check which runner your project uses before adding a test skill.

topics.name: Svelte and Astro
topics.intro: Skills for Svelte, SvelteKit, Astro and similar component frameworks. This topic collects skills written for those stacks as they are listed.
guide: Framework-agnostic frontend and design skills work with Svelte and Astro today; pair one with your framework's own documentation.
When a Svelte or Astro skill is listed, check the framework version it targets before you install it.
Use the listing request link on the topics hub to suggest a skill for this stack.

topics.name: Flutter and Dart
topics.intro: Skills for Flutter apps and Dart code, most of them official from the Flutter team: layered architecture, go_router navigation, localization, widget previews, FFI bindings, pattern matching and unit, widget and integration tests. They give an agent the conventions Flutter's maintainers recommend.
guide: Install from the Official Flutter collection first. Its skills are narrow, one task each, so you can add only the ones your app needs.
Some skills use the Dart and Flutter MCP tools to fetch runtime errors or drive the app. Read SKILL.md for the MCP server setup.
Community skills, such as flutter-dev and flutter-expert, cover state management choices like Riverpod and Bloc in one place.

topics.name: Expo and React Native
topics.intro: Skills for Expo and React Native apps, led by the official Expo collection: Expo Router, native modules in Swift and Kotlin, EAS builds, updates, hosting and app store submission, plus brownfield integration and web-to-native migration. They give an agent the current Expo workflow end to end.
guide: Start with expo-overview from the Official Expo collection. It routes each task to the skill that owns it.
EAS skills build, submit and update apps through Expo's cloud and need an Expo account and the EAS CLI; store submission also needs your Apple and Google developer credentials.
Community React Native skills and Vercel's React Native guidelines are Markdown only, so they suit any React Native project, Expo or bare.

topics.name: iOS and Swift
topics.intro: Skills for Apple platforms: SwiftUI and UIKit apps, Xcode project changes, simulator control, App Clips, Apple Human Interface Guidelines and App Store review readiness. They give an agent the platform rules an iOS team applies by habit.
guide: Most build and simulator skills need macOS with Xcode installed. Check the scripts list for the commands each one runs.
Design skills such as HIG and iOS design review are Markdown guidance and pair well with an implementation skill like swift-expert or ios-application-dev.
For cross-platform apps, the Expo skills that touch Swift (native modules, App Clips, brownfield) also appear here.

topics.name: Android and Kotlin
topics.intro: Skills for Android apps and Kotlin code: coroutines and Flow, Jetpack Compose, Apollo Kotlin, Espresso tests, Google Mobile Ads SDK integration and Google Play release delivery. They give an agent Android's build, test and release conventions.
guide: Building and testing need the Android SDK and Gradle locally. Check the scripts list on each page for what runs.
Google's Mobile Ads skills follow the current GMA SDK, including the next-gen migration, and expect an AdMob account for live ads.
Release skills prepare Play delivery; uploads need your Play Console service account, which the skill reads from your environment.

topics.name: Python
topics.intro: Skills for Python projects: modern tooling with uv, Ruff and ty, Django and FastAPI services, PyPI packaging, typing cleanup and SDK work for AWS, Dataverse and agent frameworks. They keep an agent on current Python practice for structure, types and packaging.
guide: Start with a project-wide skill such as modern-python or python-pro, then add framework skills for Django or FastAPI.
SDK skills (AWS boto3, Dataverse, LangChain, Genkit) follow that vendor's client patterns and need its credentials to run anything live.
Scientific and data libraries live in Science and Research and in Data, Analytics and Databases; this topic covers general Python engineering.

topics.name: TypeScript and Node.js
topics.intro: Skills for TypeScript and Node.js: advanced type design, Node.js best practices and core contribution, Fastify and NestJS servers, ESLint 9 flat config and TypeScript quickstarts for agent frameworks. They give an agent strict types and current Node idioms.
guide: Matteo Collina's Node.js and Fastify skills come from a Node.js core maintainer and cover type stripping, async patterns and server structure.
Pick typescript-magician or typescript-pro when generics and strictness are the hard part; both are Markdown guidance.
Framework quickstarts for LangChain, LangGraph and Genkit scaffold a project and need the matching model provider key.

topics.name: Go

guide: The eduardo-sl collection includes a router skill that maps each Go task to the skill that owns it; install the set and start there.
Review skills for concurrency and performance pair well with go-semantic-tools, which uses gopls and go list to navigate large codebases.
Generators for MCP servers and Genkit apps in Go scaffold new projects; check the module versions they pin.

topics.name: Rust
topics.intro: Skills for Rust code: idiomatic ownership and error handling, Apollo Router plugins, migrations from C++ and other languages, cargo-fuzz and security review of unsafe code. They help an agent write Rust that compiles cleanly and stays safe.

Fuzzing and unsafe-code review skills come from Trail of Bits and run cargo tooling locally.

guide: Choose by framework. Spring Boot and Quarkus each have their own application, testing and native-build skills.
Upgrade skills (JDK versions, Jakarta namespace) change many files at once; run them on a branch with your test suite ready.
Most of these are Markdown guidance from the awesome-copilot collection, so they run with your existing Maven or Gradle setup.

topics.name: PHP and Laravel

guide: Start with laravel-specialist or php-pro for application code; both cover modern PHP features.
Add a test skill that matches your runner: PHPUnit for unit tests, Dusk for Laravel browser tests, Behat or Codeception for acceptance tests.
WordPress development lives under CMS, Sanity and WordPress.

topics.name: Ruby and Rails
topics.intro: Skills for Ruby and Rails: Rails 7 Active Record tuning, Turbo Frames and Streams, RSpec and Capybara tests, Test::Unit and coverage-guided fuzzing with Ruzzy. They help an agent follow Rails conventions and test the result.
guide: rails-expert covers application code; add RSpec or Capybara skills to have tests written in the same pass.
Ruzzy from Trail of Bits runs a fuzzer locally and needs its toolchain installed.
These skills are mostly Markdown guidance and work with any Rails 7 project.

topics.name: .NET and C#
topics.intro: Skills for .NET and C#: ASP.NET Core and minimal APIs, Blazor and Fluent UI, WinUI 3 desktop apps, the MVVM Toolkit, NuGet management, .NET upgrades and MSTest, NUnit, xUnit and TUnit tests. They give an agent Microsoft's current guidance for the .NET stack.
guide: Pick by app type: ASP.NET Core skills for web APIs, Blazor skills for web UI, WinUI and MVVM Toolkit skills for desktop.
Test skills are framework specific, so match MSTest, NUnit, xUnit or TUnit to your solution.
Upgrade and containerize skills edit project files and Dockerfiles; run them on a branch.

topics.name: GraphQL and gRPC

They give an agent the schema and federation rules Apollo publishes.
guide: Start with Apollo's Official skills for any Apollo stack; they track Apollo Server 5 and Client 4.
Router and Rover skills work against GraphOS. Publishing schemas needs an Apollo graph API key, read from your environment.
For gRPC, use protobuf-grpc-api-review to check wire compatibility before you merge a .proto change.

topics.name: REST APIs and OpenAPI

They give an agent a contract-first workflow for HTTP APIs.
guide: Start from a spec. Design skills produce OpenAPI documents that the SDK, Postman and test generators then take as input.
Postman and Newman skills output import-ready collections and CI commands; running them against a live API needs its credentials.
Framework skills for Django, Fastify and ASP.NET minimal APIs also appear here when they build REST endpoints directly.

topics.name: Authentication and Login
topics.intro: Skills for adding sign-in and securing access: Firebase Auth, Amazon Cognito, Neon Auth, Sign In With Google, OAuth 2.0 and 2.1 flows, DPoP tokens, Entra ID app registration and API authentication patterns. They give an agent a checked path through identity setup, where small mistakes are costly.
guide: Use your identity provider's own skill when there is one. Firebase, AWS, Google, Neon and Microsoft skills follow that provider's current setup.
These skills touch secrets. Check the environment variables listed under Before you install and keep client secrets out of source control.
Pair an implementation skill with a security review skill before shipping a new login flow.

topics.name: Payments and Stripe
topics.intro: Skills for taking and moving money in code, mostly from Stripe: integration best practices, API version upgrades, Connect onboarding and verification, Stripe Apps, Metronome usage-based billing and agent payments, plus x402 pay-per-request setups. They keep an agent on the processor's current API.
guide: Start with stripe-best-practices, which covers sandbox and test mode planning before any live keys are involved.
Use test-mode keys while an agent works on payment code, and keep live keys out of the session environment.
x402 skills pay from a crypto wallet per request. Fund them with a small balance and read SKILL.md for the spending controls.

guide: Sanity's own collection covers schema design, content modeling, migrations and Studio upgrades; start there for any Sanity project.
WordPress skills split between development (themes, plugins, blocks) and operating a live site through the NotFair MCP, which needs that connection set up.
For a new blog on Next.js and Sanity, the building-blog skill walks through the full section, including SEO.

guide: Use the platform's Official skills first. Firebase, Supabase and Neon each publish skills that follow their current CLI and SDKs.
These skills act on live projects through each platform's CLI. Log in with a development project before you let the agent deploy.
Run the Firebase security rules auditor before launch; it checks Firestore and Storage rules for privilege escalation.

guide: shopify-expert covers themes, sections and custom apps; app work needs a Shopify Partner account and the Shopify CLI.
WooCommerce sits inside WordPress, so the WordPress skill handles store setup there.
For product photos, store SEO and sales analysis, see the e-commerce topics in Marketing and Business.

guide: Most listings are vendor-published: Google ships a large GKE set (cluster creation, autoscaling, workload identity, TPU and GPU troubleshooting) and Microsoft ships AKS skills. Choose the set for the managed service you run.

topics.name: Research
topics.intro: Skills that run research for an agent: deep web research with cited reports, investigative and primary-source researchers, literature reviews and paper lookups, hypothesis generation and scientific brainstorming, autonomous research loops, and research documentation in Notion and Google Workspace. They give an agent a method for gathering evidence and stating what it found.
guide: Match the skill to the evidence you need. Scientific skills from K-Dense-AI and Orchestra-Research work from papers and databases; general researchers (deep-research, firecrawl-deep-research, the bitwize-music researchers) work from the open web and primary sources.
Search-backed skills call a provider (Firecrawl, SerpApi, OpenAI, Gemini) and read its API key, shown under Before you install. Usage is billed by that provider.
Prefer skills that cite sources and separate fact from inference. autonomous-investigation and research-lookup structure their output that way, which makes review fast.

topics.name: Literature Search
topics.intro: Skills for finding and managing scholarly papers: searches across PubMed, arXiv, OpenAlex and other scholarly APIs, Firecrawl's research paper index, BGPT claim-level evidence, Hugging Face paper pages, citation management, Zotero libraries and systematic literature reviews. They help an agent build a reading list with real, checkable references.
guide: Pick by field. Biomedical work suits paperclip and firecrawl-research-index; ML papers suit huggingface-papers and arXiv; paper-lookup and citation-management search across many scholarly APIs at once.
Several skills call a paid or keyed service (Firecrawl, BGPT, Paperzilla, Zotero). The Before you install panel lists the variables each one reads.
Check every citation the agent returns against the source. citation-management validates metadata, and literature-review documents its search strategy so you can rerun it.

topics.name: Scientific Writing

topics.intro: Skills for writing up research: ML and systems paper drafting for venues such as NeurIPS, ICML and OSDI, scientific writing and revision, journal and conference templates, grant proposals for NSF, NIH and DOE, peer review drafts, conference posters in LaTeX and PowerPoint, and publication-quality figures. They give an agent the structure and conventions each venue expects.
guide: Start from the venue. ml-paper-writing and systems-paper-writing carry section blueprints for specific conferences, and venue-templates formats manuscripts for named journals.

Figure and poster skills run code. academic-plotting and scientific-visualization use Python plotting libraries, and latex-posters needs a LaTeX install; the scripts list on each page shows what runs.
Keep authorship decisions with the authors. Use peer-review and scholar-evaluation drafts as structured input to your own judgment, and disclose AI assistance where your venue requires it.

topics.name: Data Analysis
topics.intro: Skills for analyzing data: pandas, Polars, Dask, Vaex and cuDF DataFrames, Spark jobs, BigQuery DataFrames, exploratory analysis, read-only SQL against Postgres, MySQL and SQL Server, semantic-layer queries in Honeydew, Google Analytics reporting, Kaggle and a data scientist workflow from business question to report. They turn a question into a query, a table and a stated answer.
guide: Choose by data size and where it lives. pandas-pro and Polars suit a single machine, Dask, Spark and cuDF scale out or onto GPUs, and the BigQuery and Honeydew skills query data in place.
Skills that connect to live data read connection strings or API keys, listed under Before you install. The sanjay3290 SQL skills run read-only queries, which is the right default for analysis.
Ask for the method with the answer. data-scientist and exploratory-data-analysis report assumptions and checks alongside results, so a reviewer can follow the numbers.

topics.name: Data Visualization and Charts
topics.intro: Skills for charts and dashboards: Matplotlib and Seaborn plots, publication-ready scientific figures, HTML dashboards with KPI cards, React dashboards, Power BI model and report design, chart design guidance, and Tako charts of public data. They help an agent pick the right chart and render it cleanly.
guide: Pick by output. Matplotlib, Seaborn and scientific-visualization produce static figures for papers and reports; dashboard-creator and create-dashboard produce interactive HTML.
Power BI skills (DAX optimization, model design review, report design) assume an existing Power BI model and focus on performance and layout.
Ask the agent to render the chart and check it. Visualization skills that save and inspect the image catch unreadable labels and misleading scales before you share them.

Track experiments from the first run. huggingface-trackio, experiment-tracking-swanlab and ml-pipeline record parameters and metrics so results stay comparable.
Most skills run Python and some expect GPUs; the scripts list and SKILL.md say which. Explainability skills such as SHAP are worth adding before a model's predictions reach users.

topics.name: Notebooks
topics.intro: Skills for computational notebooks: creating and editing Jupyter notebooks, running Kaggle notebooks alongside competitions and datasets, and organizing research in an open notebook. They let an agent produce analysis people can rerun cell by cell.
guide: Use jupyter-notebook to scaffold and edit .ipynb files in a repository; it keeps cells, outputs and metadata in the format Jupyter expects.
The Kaggle skill reads your Kaggle API credentials, listed under Before you install, and acts on your account only when you ask.
Clear outputs that contain data you would not publish before you commit a notebook, and pin package versions in the first cell so the notebook reruns later.

topics.name: Bioinformatics and Genomics
topics.intro: Skills for genomics and molecular biology: single-cell analysis with Scanpy, scVI and AnnData, bulk RNA-seq and differential expression, variant and genomic interval tools, phylogenetics, CRISPR screens, protein structure and design with OpenFold, ESM, ProteinMPNN and RFDiffusion, Nextflow and Parabricks pipelines, and public databases such as CELLxGENE, DepMap and 1000 Genomes. They give an agent the procedures a computational biology lab follows.
guide: Most skills wrap one library or database. Choose by the tool your lab already uses, since the skill encodes that tool's file formats and defaults.

NVIDIA NIM skills (OpenFold, ProteinMPNN, RFDiffusion, Evo 2, MSA search) send sequences to NVIDIA-hosted endpoints and read an NGC API key. Several state this at the top of their description; check it against your data policy.
Pipelines such as Nextflow, Parabricks and DNAnexus run long jobs on compute you pay for. Start with a small sample and confirm outputs before a full run.

topics.name: Chemistry and Drug Discovery

They give an agent the cheminformatics procedures a lab trusts.
guide: Start with RDKit or Datamol for parsing and descriptors, then add a task skill (docking, property prediction, generation) on top. The task skills assume clean SMILES or SDF input.

Hosted models (NVIDIA NIM, Rowan, Tamarind) send structures to an external API and read its key, shown under Before you install. Keep proprietary compounds off hosted services your agreements do not cover.
Treat predictions as candidates for experiment. medchem filters and docking scores rank molecules; your assays decide.

Use simulation-failure-triage and hpc-runtime-doctor when a job fails. They classify the failure from logs before you change parameters.

topics.name: Physics and Quantum Computing

guide: Choose by framework and hardware. Qiskit targets IBM Quantum, Cirq targets Google Quantum AI, and CUDA-Q targets NVIDIA GPUs and QPUs; each skill follows its own SDK version.
Weather and climate skills from Earth2Studio split the work into install, data fetch, model wrappers and forecasts. Install them as a set so they hand off cleanly.
For calculations people will rely on, add uncertainty-and-units or SymPy so units and exact results are checked, and keep the script that produced each number.

Check what the skill does with output. Some save files locally, some return URLs, and some build an HTML gallery. The Before you install panel lists bundled scripts and the variables their code reads.

Specialist skills cover narrow jobs well: Bria's automotive skill handles vehicle photos, and its ad tools resize or layer a finished ad. Use them when your input matches their focus.

If background removal is one step in a bigger job, a broader skill such as Bria's e-commerce or general image skill may cover the whole pipeline in one place.
For game art, the fal.ai game development skill bundles cutouts with sprite and pixel-art generation.

guide: Upscaling here is one capability of a wider image API skill, so pick the provider you already use and confirm its upscale endpoint fits your size limits.
Both listings need a provider API key; check the cost per call before batch jobs.
For plain resizing without detail reconstruction, a local Pillow or ImageMagick skill under Image Editing is enough.

Keep one brand kit as the source of truth and point image, video and design skills at it, so every asset uses the same colors and type.

Sticker and pet skills produce small animated files with fixed size rules, so check their output format against where you will post them.

guide: Most listings use a third-party transcript API rather than Google's YouTube API, so they skip OAuth. Some are metered, so check pricing.
The ZeroPointRepo set splits by task (search, channel, playlist and transcript); install only the ones you need.
For learning, the learn-this and ship-learn-next skills turn a video into notes and an action plan.

topics.name: Short-Form Clips and Reels
topics.text_re: short-form (?:vertical )?(?:clips|video)|\breels?\b|youtube shorts|cutting long-form video into shorts|vertical promo videos
topics.intro: Skills that cut long videos into vertical clips and build Reels, Shorts and TikTok-ready promos from footage, product pages or music.
guide: Clipping skills transcribe, pick moments and reframe speakers, so they need transcription access and ffmpeg.
Reel generators start from product images or pages and often call paid animation APIs.
Check each platform's length and safe-zone rules in the skill before you post.

guide: Terminal GIF skills use VHS; PR and launch video skills use HyperFrames. Both render locally.
For polishing an existing recording, the video polish skill adds narration-synced zoom.
The automate-this skill works in reverse, turning a recording into scripts.

guide: Ad script skills start from a sourced angle; storytelling and cinematography skills plan shots and camera language.
Prompt rewriters prepare text for text-to-video models.
Most are guidance only and need no keys.

Run the finished-ad and UGC review gates before publishing.

NVIDIA VSS skills expect a deployed VSS stack.
For YouTube, a transcript skill is often enough.

topics.intro: Skills that generate songs, instrumentals and playlists with MiniMax, ElevenLabs, Venice and Suno, and turn tracks into music videos.
guide: Hosted generators need the provider's key; Suno skills write prompts you paste into Suno.
For background music under a video, choose an instrumental bed skill.
Check each provider's license terms before commercial release.
