topics.text_re: text[- ]to[- ]speech|\btts\b|voice-?overs?|\bvo\b clip|narration of|read-alouds?|listenable mp3|speech from text|speech generation
topics.intro: Skills that turn text into narration and voiceover with OpenAI, ElevenLabs, Google, Venice, NVIDIA and local models.
guide: Pick by voice and cost. Hosted skills need keys; speak-summary runs a local CPU model.
Narration skills for blogs output MP3 and embed code.
Voiceover-driven ad formats use the VO skill inside their recipe.

topics.name: Transcription and Speech to Text
topics.intro: Skills that transcribe audio and video, label speakers, and fine-tune ASR models.
guide: openai/transcribe and Venice call hosted APIs; Whisper runs locally on your hardware.
NVIDIA ASR skills target building and fine-tuning domain models.
For YouTube, fetch the existing transcript instead.

topics.name: Voice Cloning and Voice Changers
topics.text_re: clon\w* (?:a )?voice|voice clon|speech-to-speech|voice conversion|different voice|cloned or cast
topics.intro: Skills that clone a voice and convert speech to a different voice.
guide: Venice covers both cloning and voice changing through its API.
Get written consent from the speaker.
Pair with a text-to-speech skill for narration.

topics.name: Podcast Tools
topics.intro: Skills that make podcast audio from text, package podcast video with overlays, and turn podcast clips into ads.
guide: For a two-speaker episode from a blog post, use blog-audio's podcast mode.
For video podcasts, the talking-head recut adds titles and lower-thirds.
Clip-to-ad skills need hosted credits.

topics.name: Audio Editing and Mastering
topics.intro: Skills that mix, master and clean audio: stem processing, loudness, ducking and crossfades.
guide: The bitwize mix and mastering skills process Suno stems with local Python audio tools.
mix-master does an ad mix in one ffmpeg pass.
HyperFrames audio handles mixing inside a composition.

topics.name: Sound Effects
topics.intro: Skills that generate or resolve sound effects for videos and compositions.
guide: Venice audio generates effects through its API.
HyperFrames skills resolve SFX into a project.
Check license terms for each source.

topics.name: Lyrics and Songwriting
topics.intro: Skills that write, refine and review lyrics, check pronunciation and explicit content, and scan for borrowed lines.
guide: The bitwize set works as a pipeline: write, review, refine, then check before generation.
The plagiarism checker uses web search, so give it network access.
Verse craft covers poetry forms outside songs.

topics.name: Guitar and Music Theory
topics.intro: Skills for chords, guitar tabs, transposition and sheet music.
guide: clef-music-tools transposes locally and uses Clef MCP for more.
Sheet music publishing converts mastered audio into songbooks.
Publishers with guitar or theory skills can request a listing.

topics.name: Music Release and Rights
topics.name_re: release director|release linter|rights passport|sync packaging|validate album
topics.text_re: album release|distribution prep|split gaps|rights gaps|sync review|royalt|chain of title|music (?:release|distribution|licensing)
topics.intro: Skills that prepare a song or album for release: folder linting, rights audits, sync packages and release coordination.
guide: Start with the release linter to find missing files and metadata, then run the rights passport on the gaps.
Sync packaging prepares pitch materials for supervisors.
These skills prepare materials; they do not clear rights.

topics.name: Study and Exam Prep
topics.intro: Study and exam prep skills turn course material into practice an agent can run with a student. The current listings build exam-ready study plans from notes and a syllabus, and work competition math problems with step-by-step verification.
guide: Start from the material you have. Exam prep skills expect your own notes, slides or a syllabus as input, so gather those files before you ask for a plan or practice set.
For math and problem sets, pick a skill that checks its own work. Skills that verify each solution step catch the errors a single pass misses.
These skills are plain procedure with no accounts or API keys, so they are quick to install and try on one chapter before you rely on them for a full course.

topics.name: Teaching and Classrooms
topics.intro: Teaching skills help an agent run the admin side of a classroom: creating courses, managing rosters and coursework, and inviting students. The current listings work through Google Classroom.
guide: Check which platform your school uses. The Google Classroom skills call the Google Workspace CLI and need an account with teacher access to the classes they touch.
Start with read actions such as listing classes and rosters before you let an agent create courses or send invitations.
Pair a classroom skill with a document or slides skill when you want the agent to draft materials as well as post them.

topics.name: Tutoring and Courses
topics.name_re: \btutor(?:ing)?\b|educational|ship learn next|academy guide|beginner friendly tutorial|generate a tutorial
topics.intro: Tutoring and course skills turn an agent into a patient explainer: they add teaching comments to code, rewrite scripts as beginner-friendly tutorials, turn videos and articles into learning plans, and walk through compact reference implementations.
guide: Match the skill to the learner. Code tutorial skills assume a programming student; learning-plan skills work from any article or transcript you supply.
Ask for output you can check, such as a commented file, a step list or a small exercise, so the learner practices instead of only reading.
Most of these skills are Markdown with no scripts or keys. The model-implementation skills are the exception and expect a Python environment with GPU access for full runs.

topics.name: Language Learning
topics.intro: Language learning skills give an agent material to study from. The current listings pull timestamped captions and subtitles from YouTube videos so a learner can read along, translate and review foreign-language clips.
guide: Choose videos in the language and level you are studying, then ask the agent to fetch captions and build vocabulary lists or comprehension questions from them.
Caption skills depend on the video having subtitles available. Check the Before you install panel for the network access and tools they use.
Combine a caption skill with your own spaced repetition app; the skill supplies the sentences, and your app handles the review schedule.

topics.name: Health and Medical
topics.intro: Health and medical skills cover clinical documentation, medical imaging and healthcare AI pipelines. Listings include DICOM readers and converters, clinical report and treatment-plan structuring, PyHealth machine-learning pipelines and NVIDIA's clinical speech recognition workflow.
guide: Separate research tooling from clinical use. Most of these skills prepare, check or format work for licensed professionals and research teams, and their SKILL.md files state that scope.
Imaging and pipeline skills run Python against local files. Check the scripts list, and keep protected health information on systems approved for it; several DICOM skills flag PHI tags for you.
NVIDIA's healthcare skills call hosted endpoints and read an NVIDIA API key, listed under Before you install. Use de-identified data when you try them.

topics.name: Fitness
topics.intro: Fitness skills would let an agent plan workouts, read wearable data and track training. Listings that cover workouts, strength programs or devices such as Garmin and Strava land here as publishers add them.
guide: Look for skills that read your own training data through an official export or API, so plans reflect what you actually did.
Wearable integrations need an account token; the Before you install panel lists the environment variables a skill reads.
Have a plan reviewed by a qualified coach or clinician when it involves an injury or a medical condition.

topics.name: Nutrition and Recipes
topics.intro: Nutrition and recipe skills would plan meals, build grocery lists and work with recipes and calorie data. Listings that cover cooking, meal planning or nutrition data land here as publishers add them.
guide: Prefer skills that cite a nutrition database for calorie and macro figures over ones that estimate from memory.
Meal planning works best when you give the agent your constraints up front: diet, allergies, budget and the time you have to cook.
Dietary changes for a medical condition belong with a registered dietitian or physician.

topics.name: Mental Health and Wellness
topics.intro: Mental health and wellness skills would guide reflection, meditation and stress routines. Listings for mindfulness, mood tracking or wellbeing practices land here as publishers add them.
guide: Look for skills that state their scope clearly and point to professional help and crisis lines.
Plain Markdown routines are the easiest to review; read the whole SKILL.md before you use one daily.
Keep personal reflections local. Check the Before you install panel for any network access a skill uses.

topics.name: Dating and Relationships
topics.intro: Dating and relationship skills would help write profiles, plan dates and draft messages. Listings for these jobs land here as publishers add them.
guide: Profile and message skills work best from your own words; give the agent examples of how you write.
Check whether a skill connects to a dating app account, and read its permissions before you install.
Keep private details about other people out of prompts that leave your machine.

topics.name: Gift Ideas
topics.intro: Gift idea skills would turn a description of a person, an occasion and a budget into a shortlist. Listings for gift recommendations land here as publishers add them.
guide: Give the agent the recipient's interests, the occasion and a firm budget for a useful shortlist.
Skills that search live retailers read a shopping or search API key; the Before you install panel lists it.
Check prices and availability on the retailer's own site before you buy.

topics.name: Travel
topics.intro: Travel skills would plan itineraries, search flights and hotels and organize trips. Listings for trip planning and travel booking data land here as publishers add them.
guide: Prefer skills that query a live flight or hotel source, since fares and availability change by the hour.
Booking-data skills read a provider's API key; the Before you install panel lists it.
Confirm visa, entry and booking terms on the official airline, hotel or government site.

topics.name: Parenting and Kids
topics.intro: Parenting and kids skills help write for young readers. The current listings adapt stories into picture-book formats and write poems, limericks and rhymes.
guide: Give the agent the child's age and reading level so vocabulary and length fit.
Story skills work from a draft or an outline you supply, so the result stays your story.
Read every result before sharing it with a child, and keep children's personal details out of prompts.

topics.name: Personal Finance
topics.intro: Personal finance skills help an agent track money and model investments: household budget workbooks, expense trackers in Google Sheets, crypto portfolio tracking across blockchains, and stock portfolio optimization and backtesting.
guide: Decide between a local workbook and a connected account. The budget builder writes a local Excel file; portfolio trackers call a provider's API and read its key.
Crypto skills that can act on a wallet are review-first by design; read their SKILL.md and keep any signing keys out of the agent's environment.
Treat optimization and backtest output as analysis. Decisions about real money stay with you or a licensed advisor.

topics.name: Religion and Faith
topics.intro: Religion and faith skills would help with scripture study, sermon preparation and devotional writing. Listings for these jobs land here as publishers add them.
guide: Look for skills that cite the translation or source text they quote.
Sermon and study skills work best from your tradition's own materials, supplied as input.
Review drafts with your community's teachers before you share them.

topics.name: Astrology and Tarot
topics.intro: Astrology and tarot skills draw cards and read charts. The current listing draws a tarot spread to add structured randomness to vague plans, then interprets the cards for the task.
guide: Use these skills for entertainment and creative prompts; the tarot skill is built to break ties when a task is loosely specified.
It is plain procedure with no keys, so it installs and runs anywhere.
Read SKILL.md for when it triggers, so it only runs when you ask for it.

topics.name: Fun Tools
topics.intro: Fun tools are the playful side of agent skills: animated GIF stickers from photos, a Claude Code pet that sings, animated Codex pets with sprite sheets, tarot spreads and limericks on request.
guide: Sticker and singing skills call hosted image, video or music models and read an API key, listed under Before you install.
The pet and sprite skills bundle scripts that validate and package animations; check the scripts list before you run them.
These install fast and make good first skills when you are learning how skill routing works.

topics.name: Experiments and Playgrounds
topics.intro: Experiment and playground skills let an agent build quick explorers and run what-if scenarios: self-contained HTML playgrounds, structured thought experiments and research contingency analysis.
guide: Use the playground skill when you want an interactive single-file page to explore an idea; it needs no server.
Thought experiment and what-if skills are reasoning procedures, so give them a concrete decision or hypothesis to test.
All three are light installs with no keys, which makes them easy to try on a real question today.

topics.name: Sports
topics.intro: Sports skills work with live game data and fan content. The current listings advise fantasy sports start, sit and trade decisions from current player news, and generate broadcast-style fan-cam videos.
guide: Fantasy skills scrape current news through Firecrawl and read its API key; results depend on how fresh the sources are on game day.
Fan-cam video skills call a hosted video model and bill through that provider.
Check league rules and image rights before you publish generated broadcast-style video.

topics.name: Automotive
topics.intro: Automotive skills handle vehicle content. The current listing edits images of cars, trucks, SUVs and motorcycles, including scenes, reflections and tire refinement, for dealer and marketplace photos.
guide: The vehicle editing skill calls Bria's hosted image models and reads an API key, shown under Before you install.
Start from your own vehicle photos so edits stay accurate to the car being sold.
Ask for a consistent background and angle across a lot to keep inventory pages uniform.

topics.name: Agriculture
topics.intro: Agriculture skills would support farm planning, crop and livestock records and field data. Listings for these jobs land here as publishers add them.
guide: Look for skills that read your own field, sensor or yield data.
Weather and satellite data skills read a provider key; the Before you install panel lists it.
Confirm agronomic recommendations with a local extension service or agronomist.

topics.name: Nonprofits and Grants
topics.intro: Nonprofit and grant skills help prepare funding proposals. The current listing supports research grant preparation and review for NSF, NIH, DOE, DARPA and Taiwan NSTC, including opportunity fit.
guide: Give the skill the funding announcement and your project summary so it can check requirements against the actual solicitation.
Grant skills structure and review drafts; your team supplies the science, budget and commitments.
Check page limits and formatting in the agency's current guide before submission.

topics.name: Government and Public Sector
topics.intro: Government and public sector skills research official sources. The current listings retrieve court filings, government reports and public records, and research DOJ, FBI and SEC press releases and agency statements.
guide: Use these skills when a claim needs a primary source; ask the agent to return the document link with each finding.
They browse public sites, so check the network access listed under Before you install.
Confirm dates and case numbers on the agency's own site before you cite them.

topics.name: Job Search
topics.name_re: job search|job application|^apply\b|application form filler|network scan|job description analy
topics.intro: Job search skills work for the candidate: they search openings that match a resume, scan a network's companies for roles, analyze job descriptions for fit and gaps, find postings on employer career pages, and fill applications on Greenhouse, Lever and Workday.
guide: Start with a current master resume. Matching, gap analysis and application skills all read it as their source.
Search and posting skills call live data providers such as Firecrawl or LinkedIn enrichment services and read their API keys, listed under Before you install.
Review every application an agent fills before it is submitted; employers read exactly what is sent.

topics.name: Interview Prep
topics.intro: Interview prep skills get a candidate ready to talk. The current listing generates STAR stories, practice questions and talking points from a resume.
guide: Give the skill your resume and the job description together so stories map to what the role asks for.
Practice out loud with the generated questions; ask the agent to play interviewer and follow up.
It is plain procedure with no keys, so it installs anywhere.

topics.name: Career Coaching
topics.intro: Career coaching skills help a person plan their next move: translating skills across industries, optimizing a LinkedIn profile for recruiter search, comparing job offers on total compensation, and preparing salary negotiation scripts.
guide: Profile skills rewrite headline, About and Featured sections; give them your target role so the rewrite points somewhere specific.
Offer and negotiation skills need real numbers: base, bonus, equity and benefits for each offer.
Most are plain Markdown; market-rate research steps may browse the web, shown under Before you install.

topics.name: Personal Productivity
topics.intro: Personal productivity skills organize one person's day: Pomodoro timers with session tracking, recurring focus time on Google Calendar, brain dumps turned into structured plans, and a personal context portfolio the agent reads before it works for you.
guide: Calendar skills act on your Google account through the Workspace CLI; check permissions before they create events.
The personal context skill writes Markdown files about how you work, so keep them in a private folder.
Pick one capture method and one focus method, and use them daily rather than stacking overlapping skills.

topics.name: Journaling
topics.intro: Journaling skills keep a running record an agent can write to and read back. The current listing keeps a persistent desk journal that survives between sessions.
guide: Use a journal skill to carry decisions and open questions from one session to the next.
Entries are local files, so decide where they live and whether they belong in version control.
It needs no keys or network access.

topics.name: Hobbies, Home and DIY
topics.intro: Hobby, home and DIY skills would help plan projects, from 3D printing and woodworking to interior design and smart home setups. Listings for these jobs land here as publishers add them.
guide: Look for skills that work with your tools and files, such as slicer settings or smart home configs.
Smart home skills act on real devices; check the permissions and tokens listed under Before you install.
Follow manufacturer and electrical code guidance for anything that touches wiring or structure.

topics.name: Pets
topics.intro: Pet skills would help with care routines, training plans and pet health records. Listings for these jobs land here as publishers add them.
guide: Look for skills that keep records you can share with your veterinarian.
Training plans work best with your pet's age, breed and routine as input.
Health questions belong with a veterinarian.

topics.name: Events and Weddings
topics.intro: Event skills plan and run gatherings: scheduling, invitations and logistics, batch invites to calendar events, and event marketing for webinars, conferences and trade shows.
guide: Calendar and invitation skills act through Google Workspace and send real notifications, so test with a small guest list first.
The event marketing skill plans pipeline from conferences and webinars; give it your goals and budget.
Keep guest lists and contact details in your own systems, and share only what each step needs.

topics.name: Market Research
topics.intro: Skills that research a market for you: sizing, competitor monitoring and competitive intelligence, gathered from the web or a data provider and written up as a report you can act on.
guide: Check where the data comes from. Some market research skills drive a search or scraping service such as Firecrawl and need its API key; others work from what you paste in.
Pick a skill whose output matches the decision you face: a one-off market report, a recurring competitor watch, or positioning notes for a product team.
Read the sources a report cites before you rely on its numbers. The skill structures the research; the facts still come from the pages it reads.

topics.name: Press Releases and PR
topics.intro: Skills that draft press releases, media pitches and newsroom announcements in the format journalists expect, from a product launch or company news you supply.
guide: Look for a skill that asks for the facts first: who, what, when, a quote and a contact. Releases built from real details read as news, not ads.
Some PR skills also build a target media list or pitch email; choose one that matches how far you want the agent to go before you review.
Nothing should go out without your approval. These skills draft; you send.

topics.name: Newsletters
topics.intro: Skills for newsletters: writing and repurposing issues, finding newsletters to sponsor, and scanning subscriptions for signals your team can act on.
guide: Decide whether you are writing a newsletter or reading others. Writing skills draft issues from your notes; monitoring skills read an inbox and need access to it.
Inbox-reading skills connect to a mail service such as AgentMail; the Before you install panel on each page names the credential.
Sponsorship finders estimate audience and price from public pages, so treat their figures as a starting point for outreach.
